messages.content:
The `OpenMapRealMatrix` class has a `computeKey` method that calculates a key based on the specified row and column indices by multiplying the row index with the number of columns and adding the column index. 

Looking at the failing test `testMath679`, it attempts to create an `OpenMapRealMatrix` with 3 rows and `Integer.MAX_VALUE` columns. The issue report mentions an integer overflow in `computeKey()`, which is a method in the `OpenMapRealMatrix` class. This overflow occurs because the product of the row index (3) and `Integer.MAX_VALUE` exceeds the maximum value that an integer can hold.

The description in the bug report highlights that this integer overflow can occur before exhausting heap space, which could lead to unexpected behavior and potential security vulnerabilities, especially when handling access control information. 

To resolve this issue and prevent the integer overflow in `computeKey()`, the multiplication operation in the `computeKey` method needs to be handled carefully to avoid exceeding the integer range when calculating the key.

Next, I will provide the best locations to fix this issue.
The bug occurred due to an integer overflow in the `computeKey` method of the `OpenMapRealMatrix` class. To fix this issue, the multiplication operation in the `computeKey` method needs to be handled carefully to prevent exceeding the integer range.

Best locations to fix:
```
org.apache.commons.math.linear.OpenMapRealMatrix.computeKey(int, int)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
